_comment: PLACEHOLDER VALUES - do not register this as-is. Every YOUR_* and 123456789012 is a placeholder.
A Fargate task definition for the single image built by the Dockerfile at the repo root.
JSON has no comments, so the notes live in these _comment keys; the ECS API ignores unknown
top-level members, but strip them if your tooling validates strictly. What each field assumes
Register, then create a service from it (see service.json):
Assumed to exist already: an ECR repository holding the image, two IAM roles, a Secrets Manager
secret per sensitive value, and the CloudWatch log group named below. None of those are created
by registering a task definition, and three of the four are the usual reason the first task stops
before the application ever logs a line.
Both IAM roles are required and they are not interchangeable - a single role in both places is the
most common failure here. executionRoleArn is used by the ECS agent, before the container starts,
to pull the image and resolve the secrets below; without secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on those
exact ARNs the task stops during provisioning with a ResourceInitializationError and no
application logs at all. taskRoleArn is what the running process uses, and this app needs nothing
from AWS at runtime - it talks to MongoDB and to a model API - so it can be a role with an empty
policy. Keep them separate anyway: merging them hands the application permission to read its own
secrets and every other secret the execution role can reach.
_comment_size: 1 vCPU / 2 GB. Valid Fargate pairs are constrained - 1024 CPU allows 2048-8192 memory - so these
cannot be adjusted independently by arbitrary amounts. Memory is the dimension that matters: a run
holds every source's extracted text in memory while assembling one prompt (up to
LLM_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS, 600k characters) and RUN_CONCURRENCY of those can be in flight at once.
CPU is mostly idle - a run waits on somebody else's web server and on a model API - and is sized
for JVM startup rather than steady state.

containerDefinitions.name: app
_comment_image: PLACEHOLDER. The image both /harness pipelines build and push. Pin a real tag - the CI
pipeline tags with <+pipeline.sequenceId>. ECS caches nothing across task starts, so
:latest gives you a deployment you cannot reproduce and a rollback with nothing to roll
_comment_environment: Non-secret configuration, visible to anyone who can describe the task definition. Anything
sensitive belongs in `secrets` below, which resolves at start time and is not stored here.
IGNORE_HOST_CREDENTIALS is true because the host-mounted Anthropic key fallback has nothing
to read on Fargate and would only be a confusing third place for a key to come from.
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is deliberately empty: the image serves the frontend and the API from
one origin, so the shipped default (a localhost Vite dev server) would be a permitted origin
_comment_secrets: PLACEHOLDER ARNs. Each valueFrom is a Secrets Manager secret (an SSM Parameter Store
SecureString ARN works identically). The -AbCdEf suffix AWS appends to secret ARNs is part
of the ARN; copy it from the console or `aws secretsmanager list-secrets` rather than
constructing the ARN by hand. Append :key:: to pull one key out of a JSON secret.
MONGODB_URI and CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY are the two that must be set. Both have
container-local fallbacks and both fallbacks are actively wrong here: unset, the container
starts its own mongod under /data and generates its own encryption key - and a Fargate task's
filesystem is destroyed when the task stops, so every deploy, every scale event, and every
health-check restart would silently start from an empty database with an unrecoverable key.
There is no error; it looks like the app forgot everything.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is optional - an admin can add one from the Admin Console after boot, and
that override outranks this value on purpose, so a rotated key does not need a redeploy.
JWT_SECRET is deliberately absent. Unset, the app generates one on first boot, encrypts it
under CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and persists it in the database - so a task replacement does
not sign everyone out, which is exactly what supplying a rotating value here would do.
_comment_healthcheck: A container-level health check, which is not the same thing as the load balancer's. This one
decides whether ECS replaces the task; the target group's decides whether traffic reaches it.
Two caveats worth knowing before relying on this:
1. It runs INSIDE the container, so it needs curl on the image's PATH. The final stage is
Debian-based (MongoDB's server binaries need glibc), which makes curl likely but not
guaranteed. Check before shipping - `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh IMAGE -c 'command -v
curl || command -v wget'` - because a missing binary makes the check fail forever, and ECS
responds by killing a perfectly healthy task on a loop.
2. /actuator/health aggregates every health indicator, MongoDB included, so a database blip
makes this check fail and ECS replaces the task - which fixes nothing and kills every
in-flight run. If that matters more to you than catching a wedged JVM, point this at
/actuator/health/liveness (JVM state only, no Mongo) and leave the Mongo-aware check to
the target group, where failing only removes the task from rotation. The Kubernetes
sample splits them that way because Kubernetes has two separate probes for it; ECS does not.
startPeriod covers JVM boot, Mongo index verification, and the admin-seed check; failures
_comment_logs: awslogs does not create the log group unless you ask it to. Either create
/ecs/saas-investigator up front, or add "awslogs-create-group": "true" here and grant the
execution role logs:CreateLogGroup. Otherwise the task fails to start with a logging driver
error - and because the failure is in the logging driver, there is nowhere for it to say so
Worth reading on first boot specifically: the entrypoint prints a WARNING line if it had to
start an embedded MongoDB or generate an encryption key, and the app prints a loud multi-line
DEFAULT ADMIN CREDENTIAL CREATED warning the first time it seeds admin/admin against an empty
database. Either warning in a deployed environment means something above is not wired up.
_comment_readonly_root: The root filesystem is left writable, unlike the Kubernetes sample. The JVM needs a writable
java.io.tmpdir (hsperfdata at startup, library scratch files under load), and expressing that
on Fargate means readonlyRootFilesystem plus a tmpfs mount, which is more moving parts than
it is worth for a task that holds no state. Nothing is written under /data as long as
MONGODB_URI and CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY are both set above.
